title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 272
paragraphs: Moreover, I think that the women were called doves by the people of Dodona because they were Barbarians, and to the hearers it seemed that they uttered their voices like birds; but after a time (they say) the dove spoke with human voice — that is, when the woman began to speak so that they could understand her. As long as she spoke a Barbarian tongue she seemed to them to be uttering her voice like a bird — for had it really been a dove, how could it have spoken with a human voice? And in saying that the dove was black, they indicate that the woman was Egyptian. The ways of delivering oracles at Thebes in Egypt and at Dodona closely resemble one another, as it happens, and the method of divination by victims has also come from Egypt.
